name: Protein Structure Prediction
title: Protein Structure Prediction
answer: Protein structure prediction is the computational task of determining the three-dimensional shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence. The shape matters in drug discovery because it governs how a protein binds to potential drugs and to other molecules in the cell. The field covers both older template-based methods and modern deep learning approaches. This site tracks 800 scientific models, and protein structure prediction is a major category within that set.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Protein structure prediction is the computational task of determining the three-dimensional shape of a protein from its amino acid sequence. The shape matters in drug discovery because it governs how a protein binds to potential drugs and to other molecules in the cell. The field covers both older template-based methods and modern deep learning approaches. This site tracks 800 scientific models, and protein structure prediction is a major category within that set.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on graphics processing units, often in clusters or cloud environments, because training and inference involve large neural networks and many sequence alignments. Public databases such as the Protein Data Bank provide the structural data used for training and validation. Some models, including AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold, have released open source code and pretrained weights that research groups can run on their own hardware.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical pipeline starts with a protein sequence, builds a multiple sequence alignment from related proteins, and feeds that alignment into a neural network. The network predicts pairwise distances and backbone angles, which are then assembled into a three-dimensional model. Tools such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold use attention and deep residual networks to produce coordinates and per-residue confidence scores. Researchers often compare the predicted model to experimental structures from X-ray crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy when such structures exist.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The training data for these models comes largely from public repositories such as the Protein Data Bank, and the provenance of that data affects how predictions can be used. Some models are released under open licenses, while others have restrictions on commercial use, so groups need to check the terms before applying them in drug discovery. A key risk is treating a predicted structure as definitive when it has not been validated experimentally, because errors can mislead downstream design. The site's 215 compliance and regulation pages cover broader AI governance, and protein structure prediction sits within that landscape.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Newer models are extending prediction to protein complexes, nucleic acids, and small molecule interactions. The field is moving toward predicting conformational changes and dynamics, not just a single static structure. Integration with experimental methods such as cryo-electron microscopy and cross-linking mass spectrometry is an active area. For drug discovery, the hope is that faster and more accurate models will shorten the time to identify and optimize lead compounds.
